source_review.notes: Checked current official Apache Spark SQL and general tuning, Hadoop NameNode locking/metadata, Apache Parquet configuration, Apache Iceberg Spark procedures and structured streaming, Apache Flink FileSystem sink, Amazon S3 performance and prefix, and Apache Iceberg Flink maintenance documentation. All ten URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date. Sources support file-open/planning cost, namespace metadata, row-group trade-offs, checkpoint/rolling production, compaction, snapshot maintenance, request scaling, and prefix claims.

evidence: Reviewed payload bytes, file count and sizes, average size, open latency, per-file work, effective scan rate, writer/partition/checkpoint factors, snapshot and exact input/output sets, target size, compaction groups, write amplification, and benefit/cost notation.
Checked files, blocks, row groups, pages, splits, tasks, manifests, snapshots, and partitions remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Byte scopes and compressed/logical distinctions are explicitly required when reporting size or amplification.

evidence: Executed small-file-cost-model with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced 1,099,511,627,776 dataset bytes, 1,048,576 one-MiB files, 4,096 256-MiB files, and 256-fold reduction.
Reproduced modeled serial open times 8,388.608 and 32.768 seconds at eight milliseconds per file.

Reproduced abstract open-weight totals 5,497,558,138,880 and 1,116,691,496,960 bytes; recomputed exercise values 524,288 versus 4,096 files, 128-fold reduction, and 3,145.728 versus 24.576 seconds; recomputed 360,000 writer-partition-checkpoint combinations.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Serial-open and open-weight calculations are explicitly illustrative accounting, not end-to-end predictions.

evidence: Checked the first-order scan model separates payload-rate work from fixed per-file terms and skew.
Checked W times Q times C is labeled as multiplicative exposure rather than an exact output count.
Reviewed average file size, write-amplification ratio, target-by-throughput/time heuristic, exact snapshot input/output replacement, and read-benefit versus rewrite-cost comparison.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Parallel overlap and omitted coordinator/storage constraints are stated, preventing the model from being presented as exact wall time.

evidence: Reviewed empty/tiny/mixed/huge and unsplittable files, sparse and hot partitions, writer fan-out, frequent checkpoints, late data, retry, speculation, and low-volume time rolling.
Reviewed row-group extremes, dense equality/position deletes, schema/partition evolution, encryption changes, overlapping compactors, concurrent append/delete, ambiguous commit, and partial progress.
Reviewed retained snapshots, reader leases, branches/tags, clones, backups, replicas, holds, old candidates, normalized authorities, and cleanup retry.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Both new-file prevention and repair of existing layouts are covered across read, write, commit, and cleanup paths.

evidence: Traced exact snapshot input versions through compatible grouping, unique output creation, logical validation, conditional membership replacement, and delayed reference-aware cleanup.
Checked schema, rows, deletes, ordering promise, partitions, statistics, encryption, security boundary, checksums, and provenance survive compaction.
Checked writer parallelism, active partitions, rolling triggers, checkpoint cadence, buffers, and visibility remain bounded and observable.
invariant_checking.notes: Output existence never substitutes for table/manifest membership commit.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from workload measurement and producer diagnosis through target selection, prevention, exact input selection, validated output, conditional commit, reachability cleanup, and outcome measurement.

Checked counterexamples for universal size thresholds, bytes-equal-cost, capacity-equal-throughput, file-equals-task, task-coalescing-equals-layout repair, output-exists-equals-commit, row-count-equals-equivalence, age-equals-orphan, and file-count-reduction-equals-ROI.
Reviewed safe compaction proof under concurrent appends, deletes, overlapping compactors, lost commit response, and retained old-snapshot readers.
proof_review.notes: Cost benefit and data correctness are reviewed as separate obligations.

evidence: Audited uses of small, fixed, exact, atomic, immutable, safe, equivalent, live, valid, committed, retained, and orphan.
Confirmed the fixture and W*Q*C relationship are labeled as illustrative models/exposure rather than provider guarantees.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Engine and format defaults are treated as hypotheses requiring workload validation, not universal optimal values.

evidence: Reviewed file-size percentiles, request/open/footer counts, planning memory/time, tasks, scheduler delay, throughput, throttling, checkpoints, visibility, rewrite bytes, conflicts, backlog, and cleanup lag.
Confirmed no universal target size, open latency, task duration, provider throughput, compaction return, regulatory approval, or external-review claim is made.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production claims require measured engine/storage/format versions, workload distribution, query mix, concurrency, compression, security, and maintenance windows.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed workload-relative definition, fixed/variable costs, namespace and table metadata, read/write causes, streaming freshness, partitions, prevention, targets, strategies, snapshot-safe commit, validation, concurrency, cleanup, economics, observability, governance, and tests as one coherent lifecycle.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed measurement, writer fan-out, rolling policy, target interval, engine planning, table-format rewrite, exact-version commit, ambiguity resolution, retained references, orphan cleanup, ROI, security boundaries, and operational stop conditions. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from cost anatomy and producers through prevention and transactional compaction; ten examples and five complete answers cover file/open math, streaming fan-out, concurrent deletes, target experiments, and regulated cleanup.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external storage-system architect, query-engine maintainer, table-format maintainer, streaming operator, performance engineer, security auditor, records/privacy/legal specialist, research-ethics authority, or certification review is claimed.
